messages.subject: setting priors for bsem
parts:
Hi all, 

I am new to Bayesian stats and just started using  Blavaan (bsem) for my model, I am not sure if this question makes sense:

Because I have multimodal/ bimodal distributions in all of my latent variables it was suggested that I use a Dirichlet distribution for the priors in my model, is it necessary to do this in Blavaan. If so, how would I do that? 

Thank you!

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: setting priors for bsem
parts:
Elizabeth,

The bimodal distributions often indicate a problem with parameter identification. If you are fixing latent variances to 1 for identification, make sure you use the argument std.lv=TRUE when you estimate the model. Otherwise, we might be able to help more if you send the code for your model.

Also, blavaan will not automatically allow for Dirichlet priors, but I'm not sure that you would need them here.

Ed
